symptom: `mxcli init .` and `mxcli init --sync-skills .` (run at every session start by the generated SessionStart hook) overwrite an edited bundled lint rule — `Refreshed 1 bundled lint rule(s) in .claude/lint-rules/ to match this mxcli: example_microflow.star` — and, when the edit is moved to my_prefixes.star, write the stock example_microflow.star back beside it so CUSTOM002 fires from the stock list again
cause: Bundled rules were recognised by file name only: `syncBundledLintRules` rewrote any bundled-name file whose bytes differed from the binary's, and `init`'s two WalkDir loops wrote every bundled file unconditionally; neither could tell an old stock copy from a project's edit, and a missing bundled name was always recreated
file: `cmd/mxcli/lint_rules_bundled.go` (`writeBundledLintRules`, the one write path for init, init --sync-skills and add-tool), `cmd/mxcli/lint_rules_shipped.txt` (sha256 of every version ever shipped, seeded from git history); tests `cmd/mxcli/lint_rules_bundled_test.go`
insight: 'Is this file still ours?' needs the set of everything we ever shipped, not the current version: with only the current one, an unedited copy from any older mxcli is indistinguishable from an edit, and the choice is between overwriting edits and freezing every older project. The set is recoverable after the fact from git (every blob of the directory at every commit reachable from main, `git fetch --unshallow --filter=blob:none` first in a shallow clone); the v0.27.0 stock md5 in the report (cec8b599) matched one of them, which is the check that fork history covers what was released. Keep the set current with a test that the embedded version's hash is listed — it fails on the commit that changes a rule and prints the line to add. For the renamed copy, the reliable signal is the rule ID, not a manifest of names written: another file defining the bundled rule's RULE_ID is the edit moved, and it needs no state on disk, so it works for projects initialised before the fix. Normalise CRLF before hashing, or a Windows checkout of a stock rule reads as an edit. Two existing comments in shipped rules said '`mxcli init` rewrites this file' and became false with the fix — changing them is itself a new shipped version, which the currency test caught
